# The Ice House (working title)

Work-specific rules. The shared rules in the vault's `QWEN.md` and `style/` apply
first; this file only adds to them.

## Ground rules (set by the author)

1. The harbor is the protagonist's whole economy. No scene leaves the town.
2. No one explains the ice trade to anyone who works in it.

## Setting and period facts

- Penobscot Bay, Maine. The town is Sable Harbor, invented, on the east shore.
- Natural ice is cut from Sable Pond in January and February, stored in sawdust in
  the ice house, and shipped by schooner and by rail through the summer.
- A cake of ice is 22 inches square and weighs about 300 pounds.
- Electric household refrigerators reach the coast in the 1920s and take the domestic
  trade first; the fish trade holds on longer because the wharf needs bulk ice.
- The sardine cannery runs from April to November and buys ice by the ton.
- Roads to the county seat are dirt and impassable in mud season.

## Point of view and voice

- Close third person, one point-of-view character per scene.
- Odile unless a chapter says otherwise.

## The files

    README.md            what this novel is and where it stands
    bible/overview.md    logline, premise, themes, tone, structure
    bible/characters/    one file per named character
    bible/places.md      settings, buildings, roads, geography
    bible/timeline.md    year by year, real events beside invented ones
    research/            source material; names in here are NOT used in the text
    outline/             acts and chapter list; one line per chapter with status
    chapters/            NN-title.md, one file per chapter
    continuity.md        facts established in the text
    notes/               dated session logs

## Per-session order

Read `README.md`, `bible/overview.md`, `continuity.md`, `outline/`, and the latest
chapter. Draft scene by scene into `chapters/`.
